# Dylan Smith Homework 4

## Q1. Data Splitting and Reproducibility

```{r question-1-code-1}
set.seed(2026)
train.set <- sample(1:47, 35)
test.set <- setdiff(1:47, train.set)
```

## Q2. Feature Selection via ANOVA and Feature Normalization

### (a) One-Way ANOVA for Each Gene Using the Training Set

```{r question-2-code-2}
expression.matrix <- t(as.matrix(chromoX[, 3:49]))
storage.mode(expression.matrix) <- "numeric"
colnames(expression.matrix) <- make.unique(as.character(chromoX$IDENTIFIER))

training.groups <- factor(BLClabels[train.set])
anova.p.values <- apply(expression.matrix[train.set, , drop = FALSE], 2, function(x) {
  anova.table <- summary(aov(x ~ training.groups))[[1]]
  anova.table[1, "Pr(>F)"]
})

anova.results <- data.frame(
  Gene = names(anova.p.values),
  P_value = as.numeric(anova.p.values),
  row.names = NULL
)
```

### (b) Select the Five Genes with the Smallest p-Values

```{r question-2-code-3}
selected.genes <- names(sort(anova.p.values))[1:5]
selected.genes
```

### (c) Form the 47 by 5 Reduced Feature Matrix

```{r question-2-code-4}
selected.features <- expression.matrix[, selected.genes, drop = FALSE]
dim(selected.features)
```

### (d) Min-Max Normalize the Selected Features Across All Samples

```{r question-2-code-5}
feature.mins <- apply(selected.features, 2, min)
feature.maxs <- apply(selected.features, 2, max)
normalized.features <- sweep(
  sweep(selected.features, 2, feature.mins, "-"),
  2, feature.maxs - feature.mins, "/"
)
dim(normalized.features)
```

## Q3. Model Training

```{r question-3-code-6}
model.training.data <- as.data.frame(
  normalized.features[train.set, , drop = FALSE]
)
model.training.data$Class <- factor(
  BLClabels[train.set],
  levels = c(1, 2, 3),
  labels = c("BLC", "non-BLC", "Normal")
)

# Multinomial Logistic Regression
multinomial.model <- nnet::multinom(
  Class ~ ., data = model.training.data, trace = FALSE
)

# LDA
lda.model <- MASS::lda(Class ~ ., data = model.training.data)

# Naive Bayes
naive.bayes.model <- e1071::naiveBayes(
  Class ~ ., data = model.training.data
)

# K-NN
knn.training.features <- model.training.data[
  , setdiff(names(model.training.data), "Class"), drop = FALSE
]
knn.training.classes <- model.training.data$Class
knn.k <- c(4, 8, 12)

summary(multinomial.model)
lda.model
naive.bayes.model
knn.k
```

## Q4. Decision Boundary Equations

### (a) Multinomial Logistic Regression Coefficients and Decision Boundaries

```{r question-4-code-7}
multinomial.coefficients <- coef(multinomial.model)
feature.names <- setdiff(names(model.training.data), "Class")

format.multinomial.linear <- function(beta) {
  slope.terms <- sprintf("%+.6f * %s", beta[feature.names], feature.names)
  paste(sprintf("%.6f", beta["(Intercept)"]),
        paste(slope.terms, collapse = " "))
}

multinomial.boundaries <- c(
  "BLC vs non-BLC" = paste0(
    "0 = ", format.multinomial.linear(multinomial.coefficients["non-BLC", ])
  ),
  "BLC vs Normal" = paste0(
    "0 = ", format.multinomial.linear(multinomial.coefficients["Normal", ])
  ),
  "non-BLC vs Normal" = paste0(
    "0 = ", format.multinomial.linear(
      multinomial.coefficients["non-BLC", ] -
        multinomial.coefficients["Normal", ]
    )
  )
)

multinomial.coefficients
multinomial.boundaries
```

### (b) LDA Projection Directions and Decision Boundary Lines

```{r question-4-code-8}
lda.projection.directions <- lda.model$scaling
lda.projection.equations <- vapply(
  seq_len(ncol(lda.projection.directions)),
  function(j) {
    slopes <- lda.projection.directions[feature.names, j]
    paste0(colnames(lda.projection.directions)[j], " = ",
           paste(sprintf("%+.6f * %s", slopes, feature.names), collapse = " "))
  },
  character(1)
)

lda.training.scores <- predict(
  lda.model, newdata = knn.training.features
)$x
lda.class.levels <- levels(model.training.data$Class)
lda.class.means <- lapply(lda.class.levels, function(class.name) {
  colMeans(lda.training.scores[model.training.data$Class == class.name, , drop = FALSE])
})
names(lda.class.means) <- lda.class.levels

lda.within.residuals <- do.call(rbind, lapply(lda.class.levels, function(class.name) {
  class.scores <- lda.training.scores[model.training.data$Class == class.name, , drop = FALSE]
  sweep(class.scores, 2, lda.class.means[[class.name]], "-")
}))
lda.within.covariance <- crossprod(lda.within.residuals) /
  (nrow(lda.training.scores) - length(lda.class.levels))
lda.class.priors <- prop.table(table(model.training.data$Class))

lda.class.pairs <- combn(lda.class.levels, 2, simplify = FALSE)
lda.boundary.table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(lda.class.pairs, function(class.pair) {
  mean.1 <- lda.class.means[[class.pair[1]]]
  mean.2 <- lda.class.means[[class.pair[2]]]
  direction <- solve(lda.within.covariance, mean.1 - mean.2)
  intercept <- -0.5 * drop(crossprod(mean.1 + mean.2, direction)) +
    log(lda.class.priors[class.pair[1]] / lda.class.priors[class.pair[2]])

  data.frame(
    Class_1 = class.pair[1], Class_2 = class.pair[2],
    LD1 = direction[1], LD2 = direction[2], Intercept = intercept,
    Equation = sprintf("%.6f * LD1 %+.6f * LD2 %+.6f = 0",
                       direction[1], direction[2], intercept)
  )
}))

lda.projection.directions
lda.projection.equations
lda.boundary.table
```

## Q5. Visualization of Decision Boundaries

### Choose Two Features and Create a Prediction Grid

```{r question-5-code-9}
plot.features <- colnames(knn.training.features)[1:2]
grid.resolution <- 140
feature1.values <- seq(0, 1, length.out = grid.resolution)
feature2.values <- seq(0, 1, length.out = grid.resolution)
prediction.grid <- expand.grid(
  feature1.values,
  feature2.values
)
names(prediction.grid) <- plot.features

training.feature.means <- colMeans(knn.training.features)
grid.data <- as.data.frame(lapply(training.feature.means, function(value) {
  rep(value, nrow(prediction.grid))
}))
names(grid.data) <- names(training.feature.means)
grid.data[[plot.features[1]]] <- prediction.grid[[plot.features[1]]]
grid.data[[plot.features[2]]] <- prediction.grid[[plot.features[2]]]

class.colors <- c(
  "BLC" =  "lightblue",
  "non-BLC" = "white",
  "Normal" = "grey"
)
training.classes <- knn.training.classes
```

### Plot Decision Regions and Training Points

```{r question-5-code-10}
plot.class.regions <- function(predicted.classes, plot.title) {
  region.matrix <- matrix(
    as.integer(predicted.classes),
    nrow = length(feature1.values),
    ncol = length(feature2.values)
  )

  image(
    x = feature1.values, y = feature2.values, z = region.matrix,
    col = unname(class.colors), breaks = seq(0.5, 3.5, by = 1),
    xlab = plot.features[1], ylab = plot.features[2],
    main = plot.title, useRaster = TRUE
  )
  contour(
    x = feature1.values, y = feature2.values, z = region.matrix,
    levels = c(1.5, 2, 2.5), add = TRUE, drawlabels = FALSE,
    col = "black", lwd = 1.2
  )
  points(
    knn.training.features[[plot.features[1]]],
    knn.training.features[[plot.features[2]]],
    pch = 19, col = class.colors[as.character(training.classes)]
  )
  legend(
    "topright", legend = names(class.colors),
    fill = unname(class.colors), title = "Predicted class", cex = 0.8
  )
}

lda.grid.classes <- predict(lda.model, newdata = grid.data)$class
plot.class.regions(lda.grid.classes, "LDA Decision Regions")

naive.bayes.grid.classes <- predict(
  naive.bayes.model, newdata = grid.data, type = "class"
)
plot.class.regions(naive.bayes.grid.classes, "Naive Bayes Decision Regions")
```

### K-NN Decision Regions for k = 4, 8, 12, and 5

```{r question-5-code-11}
knn.plot.values <- c(4, 8, 12, 5)
knn.grid.classes <- setNames(
  lapply(knn.plot.values, function(k) {
    class::knn(
      train = knn.training.features,
      test = grid.data,
      cl = knn.training.classes,
      k = k
    )
  }),
  paste0("k = ", knn.plot.values)
)

for (model.name in names(knn.grid.classes)) {
  plot.class.regions(
    knn.grid.classes[[model.name]],
    paste("K-NN Decision Regions (", model.name, ")", sep = "")
  )
}
```

## Q6. Test Set Evaluation & Performance Comparison

### (a) Holdout Predictions and Confusion Matrices

```{r question-6-code-12}
test.features <- as.data.frame(
  normalized.features[test.set, , drop = FALSE]
)
class.levels <- levels(model.training.data$Class)
test.classes <- factor(
  BLClabels[test.set], levels = c(1, 2, 3),
  labels = c("BLC", "non-BLC", "Normal")
)

test.predictions <- list(
  "Multinomial Logistic Regression" = predict(
    multinomial.model, newdata = test.features, type = "class"
  ),
  "LDA" = predict(lda.model, newdata = test.features)$class,
  "Naive Bayes" = predict(
    naive.bayes.model, newdata = test.features, type = "class"
  ),
  "K-NN (k = 4)" = class::knn(
    train = knn.training.features, test = test.features,
    cl = knn.training.classes, k = 4
  ),
  "K-NN (k = 8)" = class::knn(
    train = knn.training.features, test = test.features,
    cl = knn.training.classes, k = 8
  ),
  "K-NN (k = 12)" = class::knn(
    train = knn.training.features, test = test.features,
    cl = knn.training.classes, k = 12
  )
)
test.predictions <- lapply(test.predictions, function(x) {
  factor(as.character(x), levels = class.levels)
})

multiclass.confusion.matrices <- lapply(test.predictions, function(predicted) {
  table(
    Actual = factor(test.classes, levels = class.levels),
    Predicted = factor(predicted, levels = class.levels)
  )
})
for (method in names(multiclass.confusion.matrices)) {
  cat("\n", method, "\n", sep = "")
  print(multiclass.confusion.matrices[[method]])
}

binary.levels <- c("Non-normal", "Normal")
actual.binary <- factor(
  ifelse(test.classes == "Normal", "Normal", "Non-normal"),
  levels = binary.levels
)
to.binary.class <- function(x) {
  factor(ifelse(x == "Normal", "Normal", "Non-normal"), levels = binary.levels)
}
binary.confusion.matrices <- lapply(test.predictions, function(predicted) {
  table(Actual = actual.binary, Predicted = to.binary.class(predicted))
})
for (method in names(binary.confusion.matrices)) {
  cat("\n", method, " (Normal is positive)\n", sep = "")
  print(binary.confusion.matrices[[method]])
}
```

### (b) False Positives, False Negatives, Precision, Recall, and F1-Score

```{r question-6-code-13}
performance.results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(binary.confusion.matrices), function(method) {
  confusion <- binary.confusion.matrices[[method]]
  true.negative <- confusion["Non-normal", "Non-normal"]
  false.positive <- confusion["Non-normal", "Normal"]
  false.negative <- confusion["Normal", "Non-normal"]
  true.positive <- confusion["Normal", "Normal"]

  precision <- if (true.positive + false.positive == 0) {
    NA_real_
  } else {
    true.positive / (true.positive + false.positive)
  }
  recall <- if (true.positive + false.negative == 0) {
    NA_real_
  } else {
    true.positive / (true.positive + false.negative)
  }
  f1.score <- if (2 * true.positive + false.positive + false.negative == 0) {
    NA_real_
  } else {
    2 * true.positive /
      (2 * true.positive + false.positive + false.negative)
  }

  data.frame(
    Method = method,
    FP = as.integer(false.positive), FN = as.integer(false.negative),
    Precision = as.numeric(precision), Recall = as.numeric(recall),
    F1 = as.numeric(f1.score),
    row.names = NULL
  )
}))

knitr::kable(
  performance.results, digits = 3,
  caption = "Holdout performance for Normal (positive) vs. Non-normal"
)
```
